name: @argszero/dsh-legacy-prompt-vars
description: Keep a profile that was written against an older dsh release from failing every turn with `unknown prompt variable "{{cwd}}"`. Discussions #9962 and #9948 report that after upgrading, every run dies before any model request: `unknown prompt variable "{{cwd}}" in section "deployment:persona-suffix"; registered variables: provider, model`. The interpolation in packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts is strict by design — an unregistered name is not left as literal text, it throws during request assembly — and 0.2.0-rc.2 was the last release that registered `cwd` (packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:372 `ctx.systemPrompt.variable('cwd', context => context.agent?.session.header.cwd)`). Commit 79bd3d8da7 (feat(session): centralize working directories and directory context, first tagged dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2, not an ancestor of dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2) removed that registration and the factory `personaSuffix: Your working directory is {{cwd}}.` together, and replaced the duty with the required runtime context `working-directory:current` (packages/session/working-directory/src/index.ts). So a `{{cwd}}` reference can only come from a layer an upgrade does not rewrite — the profile's own cordis.patch.yml, the home patch, or a preset row — and there it is frozen permanently, because the config editor writes a whole `config` object back (packages/boot/config-editor) rather than the one field that was edited. The real repair is to delete that line from the file `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` names, and the upstream fix is to clean dead references at load time or stop materializing defaults into the user layer. What a plugin can do is register the missing name, because `ctx.systemPrompt.variable(name, provider)` is a public API and nothing in the current tree registers `cwd`. This plugin registers exactly that one name — the pre-removal variable set was exactly `cwd`, verified by a full grep of the dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2 tag — reading the effective working directory from the `workingDirectory` service, then the session header, then a launch-directory fallback, and it never returns undefined and never throws, because either would only replace one fatal assembly error with another. Zero runtime dependencies.
